newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich sees victory on U.S. tax bill goals.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich sees victory on U.S. tax bill goals.

text.p: U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Tuesday he believed Republicans would prevail on five key points in tax bill negotiations with the Clinton administration.
In a speech to a farm group, Gingrich also supported eventual elimination of the capital gains and estate taxes.
Gingrich and other Republican leaders were to meet with President Clinton later in the day to discuss tax issues.

During a breakfast speech to state Farm Bureau presidents, Gingrich said he would argue at the White House meeting that "tax cuts should be given to taxpayers" -- a reference to a major dispute with Clinton over the scope of tax cuts.
Gingrich said Republicans also would press for a $500 per child tax credit, tax deductions for education, reduction in the capital gains tax rate and a larger exclusion from estate taxes.
"I think by the time we get done negotiating, we are going to get these targets," Gingrich said, adding that Clinton would get some of his priorities too.

The Clinton administration has argued the $500 per child tax credit ought to be available to all families, including those who receive the earned income tax credit. Gingrich said the EITC in some cases amounted to a $1,000 check to families so it would be improper to give them the $500 credit when they did not pay any income taxes.
He said the EITC had a high error rate, as much as 21 percent, which would make Clinton's proposal costly due to potentially billions of dollars in overpayments.
"That's where he wants your tax cuts to go," Gingrich said. "I'm going to ask him today how he could possibly want to do that."
Also during his speech, Gingrich said he believed a "flat" tax or a consumption tax would emerge in the next few years as a replacement to the federal income tax.
